newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aalsmeer flower market '96 profits 17.6 mln guilders.
newsitem.headline: Aalsmeer flower market '96 profits 17.6 mln guilders.

text.p: Bloemenveiling Aalsmeer (VBA), the world's largest flower market, made a profit of 17.6 million guilders in 1996, a 30 percent rise on the previous year.
Revenue increased nearly 140 million guilders to 2.6 billion guilders, an increase of 5.7 percent on 1995 levels, the market said in its annual statement.
VBA said the positive result was due to the exceptionally good weather of last year as the cool summer boosted flower production after the heat waves of the two previous years, it added.
The largest revenue rise increase took place in the garden plants sector with a 12 percent, while cut flowers rose by five percent and house plants by six percent in revenue terms.
Cut flowers in 1996 totalled four billion pieces and 500,000 plants were handled by Aalsmeer.

Roses, tulips and chrysanthemums were the favourites. In revenue, roses, the lead export, accounted for 600 million guilders, with Germany -- the auction largest export market -- increasing flowers purchase from VBA..
Exports from all of the Netherlands flower markets to Germany represented 2.2 billion guilders in revenue last year.
The market is also investing 135 million guilders in an expansion of VBA-South due to increasing space demands from traders.
Aaslmeer now has a trading area of 750,000 sq m and this is being increased by a further 300,000 sq m.
The market is also building a larger cash and carry centre and an area where the Dutch exporters can build their own facilities to operate from.
Growth in foreign production led to a smaller global market share for the Dutch flower industry, VBA said..

The Netherlands has a 60 percent world market share in flower exports. A spokeswoman said that last year Dutch production did not grow as fast as international levels. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017 --www.racs.com
